name: Kalundborg
title: Kalundborg Tanker and Bulk Ship UTM | Thickness Gauging
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Kalundborg for crude and product tankers at the refinery jetty, bulk carriers and ro-ro ships: ballast tanks, decks, piping.
h1: Thickness Gauging for Refinery Tankers and Bulk Carriers at Kalundborg
intro: Kalundborg, on the west coast of Zealand, is an industrial harbour built around a refinery, a power station and some of Denmark's largest process plants. Crude and product tankers use the refinery's jetty, bulk carriers serve the power station and the town's industry, and ro-ro and general cargo ships work the public quays, with a ferry to Samsø adding local traffic. Long tanker and bulk stays here give realistic gauging windows. For each job, Atlantis sends technicians from India to join the ship at her berth.

highlights.p: Crude oil reaches the Kalundborg refinery by sea and refined products leave on smaller tankers. While cargo is worked, cargo tanks stay shut, but segregated ballast tanks, the forepeak, void spaces and deck structure can often be measured with the terminal's agreement.

highlights.h: Raw materials for an industrial cluster
highlights.p: Kalundborg's process plants and power station are linked in the well-known Kalundborg Symbiosis, and many of their bulk inputs arrive by sea. Bulk carriers discharging at the industrial quays give access to their holds one at a time as each is emptied.

highlights.h: Close to the Great Belt route
highlights.p: Kalundborg lies a short way off the deep-water route that large ships follow between the Kattegat and the Great Belt. Superintendents with ships trading through Danish waters can use a Kalundborg call for readings without a long deviation from the voyage.

port.h: Kalundborg's fjord harbour on Zealand's west coast
p: Kalundborg stands at the head of Kalundborg Fjord, an inlet sheltered by the Røsnæs peninsula to the north and the Asnæs peninsula to the south, opening westwards towards the Great Belt and the Kattegat. The fjord is naturally deep, which is one reason a refinery and a power station were built on its shores and why large ships can berth close to industry without a long dredged approach. The large-ship route through the Great Belt passes a short distance offshore, so tankers and bulk carriers reach the port with only a brief turn away from their passage. Ice is rare in the fjord, and with the small tidal range of these waters, berthing is governed by wind and pilotage rather than by the tide.

The refinery, owned since 2021 by the Klesch Group after decades under Statoil and Equinor, receives crude by tanker and ships out refined products, and it is the largest single source of tanker calls. At Asnæs, the power station has moved from coal to biomass, bringing wood-fuel and other bulk deliveries by sea. Novo Nordisk, Novonesis and other process plants form the core of the Kalundborg Symbiosis, a network in which surplus energy, water and by-products pass between companies, and the public port handles bulk, project cargo and ro-ro traffic for them and for the wider region. The ferry to Samsø completes the picture, running a regular service across the water to the island and keeping its own timetable at the ferry berth.

Port stays follow the industries they serve. A crude tanker discharging at the refinery stays for the length of her pumping, product tankers berth for loading, and bulk carriers delivering to the power station or the process plants discharge over one or more days depending on cargo and equipment. Ro-ro ships and the Samsø ferry run to timetables. For inspection, the long bulk and tanker stays are the most useful, while the refinery's safety regime and the industrial sites' own rules shape how work is organised aboard and on the quay. A tanker kept waiting for her berth, or held alongside after cargo while documents or orders are settled, can give extra hours that a prepared scope can put to good use.

facilities.h: Where gauging is done at Kalundborg
p: Kalundborg is an industrial harbour rather than a repair port, so ships are gauged afloat at their working berths. At the refinery jetty, the terminal's rules govern everything the team brings and does: equipment is cleared in advance, enclosed-space entry follows the ship's permit system, and work on deck keeps away from the manifold during cargo transfer. The bulk quays give more freedom. Holds can be measured as each one is emptied and swept during discharge, and on a ship loading at the port the ballast tanks become reachable once they have been pumped out and the crew has ventilated them.

Ships trading to Kalundborg go elsewhere for dry-docking. Fayard at Lindø on Funen is the closest large repair yard, a short passage across the Great Belt, and Ørskov Yard in Frederikshavn and yards in Poland and Germany are other common choices. Measuring ballast tanks and deck during a Kalundborg call before a docking lets the superintendent give the yard a firmer steel estimate. Ships lying at a waiting berth for cargo or between charters are the best candidates for longer pre-purchase or condition gauging, since the crew can open spaces in turn without cargo work getting in the way.
list: Refinery crude and product jetty — ballast tank, forepeak, void-space and deck gauging on tankers during cargo operations, under terminal rules.
Power station bulk quay at Asnæs — hold and tank-top readings on bulk carriers discharging biomass fuel.
Public port bulk and project quays — holds, ballast tanks and deck on bulk and general cargo ships alongside.
Ro-ro berths — vehicle-deck, ramp and ballast tank measurement on ro-ro ships during scheduled port time.
Waiting berths in the harbour — pre-purchase and on-hire condition gauging on idle ships.
Fayard dry docks, Lindø — shell and bottom gauging when a Kalundborg trader goes to dock on Funen.

context.h: Refinery tankers, vetting and port state control at Kalundborg
p: Port state control in Kalundborg is the work of the Danish Maritime Authority under the Paris MoU, and tankers calling at a refinery attract attention from several directions at once. Alongside the PSC risk profile, charterers and the terminal's ship-acceptance process look at vetting reports and the ship's structural history, and a tanker with recent corrosion findings may be asked for evidence of repairs or fresh measurements before she is fixed again. Thickness readings set out against the allowable diminution for each member are the kind of evidence those reviews look for.

Kalundborg's industry is also in transition. The Symbiosis companies are investing in lower-carbon production, the power station has left coal behind, and EU climate rules now reach shipping through the ETS, applied from 2024, and FuelEU Maritime, applied from 2025. Ships of 500 GT and above that call at Danish ports must also carry a valid Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation. For owners of older tankers and bulk carriers on Danish and Baltic trades, these rules change the case for keeping ageing ships, and gauging data from a Kalundborg call helps show whether the next renewal survey is worth the steel it will demand.

jobs.p: Kalundborg jobs are usually built around a cargo operation. For a tanker, the scope is set by what the ship can make gas-free during her stay at the jetty; for a bulk carrier, by the order in which holds come free during discharge and the time left before she sails. The superintendent fixes the list, the crew prepares the spaces, and the team works through them with readings reported as each is finished, so an owner can decide on repairs, further inspection or a docking while the ship is still in port. Renewal-survey programmes for these ships are normally completed at the docking yard, with Kalundborg used for preparatory readings. Examples:
list: Segregated ballast tank and forepeak gauging on a crude tanker discharging at the refinery, ahead of her renewal survey docking.
Measurement of deck cargo lines and their supports on a product tanker lifting refinery output, at a charterer's request.
Hold frame and tank-top gauging on a bulk carrier discharging wood fuel for the power station.
Ramp and vehicle-deck measurement with crack detection at the hinges on a ro-ro ship during scheduled port time.
On-hire condition gauging on a product tanker lying at a waiting berth before delivery to a new charterer.

logistics: Copenhagen Airport is the natural arrival point for Kalundborg, with a regional rail line running west across Zealand to the town and road transfers as an alternative. The refinery jetty and industrial quays sit behind ISPS-controlled gates, and the refinery adds its own safety induction, so the ship's agent passes the team's details to the terminal in advance. Technicians come from India on Schengen visas, and because tanker berthing windows can shift, we confirm travel against the agent's latest berthing prospect rather than the first estimate.
vessels: General cargo and project cargo ships
Ro-pax ferry on the Samsø route

faqs.q: What can be gauged on a tanker at the Kalundborg refinery jetty?
faqs.a: Spaces outside the cargo system that the ship can certify safe: segregated ballast tanks, the forepeak, void spaces and cofferdams, and deck plating away from the manifold. Cargo tanks stay closed while the ship is working cargo. Every item, from the gauges to the route along the deck, is agreed in advance with the master and the terminal, and the work pauses whenever the terminal's operations require it.

faqs.q: How do Kalundborg readings feed into a later docking?
faqs.a: Each reading is tied to a frame, strake and location on the TM plan, so the yard and the attending surveyor can use a Kalundborg set of readings directly when the ship docks, whether at Fayard on Funen, in Poland or further afield. The steel estimate built from those readings can go into the yard specification before arrival, and the team can rejoin the ship in dock to finish the shell and bottom.

faqs.q: Can bulk carriers discharging biomass be gauged hold by hold?
faqs.a: Yes, once each hold has been emptied and cleaned enough for the steel to be seen and prepared. Wood pellets and chips leave dust and residues that have to be removed at the reading points, so the crew's cleaning and the stevedores' sequence decide when each hold is ready. Frames, brackets, hopper plating and the tank top are the usual focus on these ships.

faqs.q: Does the Kalundborg Symbiosis affect access to the quays?
faqs.a: Indirectly. The industrial sites around the harbour run their own safety and access systems on top of the port's ISPS controls, and some quays serve a single plant. The ship's agent knows which rules apply at each berth and arranges passes and inductions for the team, so we ask for the berth name as early as possible when planning the job and adjust the team's paperwork to match.
